output.summary: Track search filter usage and whether filtered searches lead to result clicks. This builds on the existing search events and does not redefine searches. (1) A new event, search_filter_applied, fires each time a user changes a filter on the results page. It answers 'which filters do people use'. (2) search_performed and search_result_clicked are extended with optional filter-state properties and a client-generated search_id. A click can then be attributed to a filtered or unfiltered result set, and to the specific filters active at click time. Changing a filter must NOT fire another search_performed. If it did, the search_success_rate denominator would inflate. The filter change is captured only by search_filter_applied.
clarifying_questions: Is the price range a set of preset buckets (e.g. 'under $50', '$50–$100') or a free min/max slider? If buckets, I'd swap filter_price_min/max for an enum of bucket ids.
Can users select more than one category at once? The spec uses an array to cover both cases, but confirm so engineering can validate it.
Do you also need filter removals and 'clear all' tracked, or only filters being applied? This spec includes a filter_action of applied/removed/cleared; drop it if removals don't matter.

Are the filters live in the iOS/Android apps as well as web, or web only? Older app versions won't send the new optional properties, so filtered-vs-unfiltered comparisons should be limited to versions that do.

events.name: search_filter_applied
events.trigger: Fires once when the user changes a search filter on the search results page (category, price range, or in-stock toggle) and the updated result set has loaded. It fires on apply, remove, and clear-all. It does not fire on initial page load when filters are pre-set from the URL; that state is captured on search_performed instead.
events.description: A user changed a filter on a search results page. It records which filter changed and the full filter state after the change. It must not trigger a search_performed event.

properties.name: search_id
properties.description: Client-generated id of the current search, matching the search_id on the search_performed event for this query.

properties.name: filter_type
properties.description: Which filter the user changed. Use 'all' for a clear-all action.

properties.name: filter_action
properties.description: Whether the filter was set or changed (applied), unset (removed), or all filters were reset (cleared).

properties.name: filter_categories
properties.description: Category filter values active after the change, as internal category slugs (array of strings). Omit or send empty when no category filter is set.

properties.name: filter_price_min
properties.description: Lower bound of the active price filter after the change, USD. Omit when not set.

properties.name: filter_price_max
properties.description: Upper bound of the active price filter after the change, USD. Omit when not set.

properties.name: filter_in_stock_only
properties.description: Whether the in-stock-only toggle is on after the change.

properties.name: active_filter_count
properties.description: Number of filter types active after the change (0-3).

properties.name: results_count
properties.description: Number of results shown after the filter change.

events.name: search_performed
events.trigger: Unchanged: fires when the user submits a search query. It must NOT fire again when only filters change.
events.description: Adds a search_id for joining to filter and click events, plus the filter state at submit time. Filters can already be active when the search is submitted, e.g. persisted from a prior search or set via URL.

properties.name: search_id
properties.description: Client-generated UUID created when the query is submitted. Reuse it on all filter and click events for this query until a new query is submitted.

properties.name: is_filtered
properties.description: True if any filter is active when the search is submitted.

properties.name: filter_categories
properties.description: Active category filter slugs at submit time (array of strings).

properties.name: filter_price_min
properties.description: Active price filter lower bound at submit time, USD.

properties.name: filter_price_max
properties.description: Active price filter upper bound at submit time, USD.

properties.name: filter_in_stock_only
properties.description: Whether the in-stock-only toggle is on at submit time.

events.name: search_result_clicked
events.trigger: Unchanged: fires when the user clicks a search result.
events.description: Adds the search_id and the filter state at click time, so clicks can be attributed to filtered vs unfiltered result sets and to specific filters.

properties.name: search_id
properties.description: search_id of the search this click belongs to.

properties.name: is_filtered
properties.description: True if any filter was active when the result was clicked.

properties.name: filter_categories
properties.description: Active category filter slugs at click time (array of strings).

properties.name: filter_price_min
properties.description: Active price filter lower bound at click time, USD.

properties.name: filter_price_max
properties.description: Active price filter upper bound at click time, USD.

properties.name: filter_in_stock_only
properties.description: Whether the in-stock-only toggle was on at click time.

kpi_links.reason: Both of its events (search_performed, search_result_clicked) gain new properties. The definition is unchanged if filter changes do not fire search_performed. If engineering instead fires search_performed on each filter change, the denominator inflates and the rate drops. Growth may also want to segment the KPI by is_filtered once data accrues; filtered and unfiltered numbers will only be complete for app versions that send the new properties.

output.privacy_notes: Filter values are product attributes, not personal data, so the new properties carry no PII. Send category filters as internal category slugs, not display text. The new search_filter_applied event deliberately uses search_id instead of repeating the free-text query. This avoids copying user-typed text, which could contain names, emails or phone numbers, into another event. The existing query property on search_performed and search_result_clicked has that risk today. Consider scrubbing email- and phone-like patterns client-side before sending. search_id must be a random UUID per query and must not be derived from any user or device identifier.
